original.target_description: Published Schmeichel (2007), Experiment 1, pp. 243–244: attention-control versus no-control conditions; operation-span and sentence-span performance standardized within test type and analyzed together. Page 244 reports four separate recall endpoints plus distractor performance and a manipulation check. The supplied description and page locator do not uniquely identify one outcome/test.

notes: Fresh original-only blind validation. Published article title, author, year, journal and DOI verified against supplied primary source. Source version: published article supplied by licensed EBSCO PsycInfo service. Original source: /home/lukas/.t3/worktrees/fred-data/audit-fred-stats-2026-10/audit/fred_stats_2026-10/texts/followup_mac_32fd76ba5dde685e762284a3.txt. PDF cross-check: /home/lukas/work/fred-mac-recovery-20261030/private_batch_01/artifacts/32fd76ba5dde685e762284a3_ebsco_psycinfo.pdf. Experiment 1 Method (p. 243) identifies a final sample of 141 undergraduate participants after excluding four who tried to memorize distracting words; this sample applies to the combined recall analyses. However, p. 244 separately reports individual-word recall, correctly recalled sets, total words in correctly recalled sets, and longest correctly recalled set, each with its own F, p and d. The input does not identify which of these endpoints is assigned; no test was selected from input order, requested metric, or replication reference. Statistic fields remain null because a unique test cannot be established. The supplied broad description also mentions reverse digit span and response inhibition, which are not the Experiment 1 recall outcomes. No original statistics were taken from replication sources. Reported success and replication were not assessed because target_side is original.
